question: Can a causal local-level Kalman filter on the model's own two output streams reduce prediction noise without changing model weights or reading labels at inference?
scope: CPU-only postprocessing screen of one pinned full-validation parent prediction cache on the repeatedly exposed F0 panel

evaluation.warmup_rows: 0..98; available predictions may initialize/calibrate the state, but target and mask values are not read for filtering
evaluation.exposure: Previously inspected F0 endpoints and labels; discovery screen only, not clean validation

prefix_moments_q_over_r.q_over_r_source: first 99 model predictions for each sequence and target channel; no target or mask

prediction_contract.scored_row_causality: Rows 0..98 are unscored calibration/warmup. The adaptive gain is estimated from predictions 0..98, then applied to the sequence; every scored output at row 99 or later uses only the calibrated prefix and predictions up to its current row.

grading.limitations: All F0 endpoints and labels were previously exposed; intervals condition on fixed predictions and do not estimate training-seed or public-transfer uncertainty.

screen_interpretation.strong_follow_up_signal: At least +0.001 pooled WP over raw parent and nonnegative direction in at least three of four descriptive component folds.
screen_interpretation.rule_scope: A follow-up prioritization heuristic only; a negative or uncertain screen does not reject other Kalman, online-learning, teacher, or student mechanisms.
screen_interpretation.b300_handoff: This is a fixed-model CPU postprocessing screen, not a large-scale training direction. A result alone does not authorize a B300 draft.
